items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Because see, Brown was one of the original guys in the Missourians, and They didn't want to insult him. So they switched it around to "You sound better on the alto than Walter does, and we'll let him play tenor."

ctx.x: I'd been listening all the time he was playing. Because Brown was a little from the old school, he was a little on the corny side. But I'd heard Lester Young and Chu Berry and all them guys, and I had that modern way of playing. So I picked up the tenor and I started to play the solo -- the guys couldn't understand how I could play them (?). At one time, I could play anything I heard. If I heard the chord, I could play it. So sitting there and playing with a guy, you dug what the chord was.

So when Brown came back, they talked Brown into the idea that he sounded better on alto than I did. They didn't say I sounded...because they didn't want... Because see, Brown was one of the original guys in the Missourians, and They didn't want to insult him. So they switched it around to "You sound better on the alto than Walter does, and we'll let him play tenor." And that was the beginning of me playing tenor. That's how I got on the tenor.

And then we started this thing on the air... And Cab really made me famous. It wasn't me. I played them solos, and he'd say, "Play it, Foots!" and I'd be playing the best I could. And I'd just keep playing all that stuff I knew, because playing with Jelly... See, if you play with New Orleans guys, that stuff gets in your head. Because I'd also played with Luis Russell, you know.
